caveats: A shadow fill assumes the aggressor would have traded the same size against the shadow and that nobody reacted to it; real fill rates may differ in an unknown direction.
The L3 reference follows displayed orders only; hidden and reserve interest is invisible.
A replace is treated as losing priority and file order as time order inside a nanosecond (shared interpretations of the specification).
Fill = first counterfactual execution of any part of the 100-share shadow (first touch).
Differences between models measure dependence on unobservable queue position; they do not say which model is right outside these data.
Shadows have overlapping horizons and serial dependence; nominal 95% Wilson, Newcombe and Greenwood intervals do not account for this dependence, and their coverage is not established.
Hypothesis decisions are nominal/exploratory and unadjusted for multiple comparisons; rejection counts cannot be interpreted as what chance would produce under these dependent comparisons.

clock.basis: nanoseconds since the synthetic session's midnight; frame order
clock.local_clock: absent: every latency is the swept assumption L

rules: Messages are processed in stream (file) order; messages sharing a timestamp are never reordered.
Shadow k is scheduled at window_start + k * interval for every such time before window_end; even k is a buy, odd k a sell. Its arrival is the scheduled time plus the latency L.
A shadow arriving at T is sequenced after every message stamped before T and before the first message stamped at or after T; arrivals at or after window_end are not placed.
At arrival it joins the back of the displayed best queue of its side at that price; it is not placed when that side is empty or the book is locked or crossed at that moment.
No impact: the shadow is never added to the book and no message is changed because of it.

L3 reference: shares ahead are the displayed shares at the price at arrival; executions, cancellations, deletes and replaces of those orders reduce them. A replace loses priority: its new order is behind.

L3 fill: an execution (E or C, printable or not) of a displayed order on the shadow's side at its price that was not ahead of it (queue), or at a worse price (trade-through); or the opposite best reaching its price after a message (book cross).

L2 projection: a displayed printable execution emits a trade row (aggressor opposite the resting side) before its depth row; each changed level emits a depth row with the new total; non-printable executions, non-cross trades (P) and crosses (Q) emit no sided row and are ignored, as by hftbacktest's NoPartialFillExchange.

L2 models: hftbacktest 0.9.4 formulas (docs/QUEUE_MODELS.md), lot size 1 share. front starts at the displayed quantity at arrival; a trade at the price calls trade then is_filled (fill when round(-front) > 0); a trade at a better price fills (trade-through); a depth row at the price calls depth(prev, new); the opposite best reaching the price fills (book cross).
A fill is the first counterfactual execution of any part of the shadow (first touch).

Each shadow is followed until every path filled, until its longest horizon or checkpoint passed, or until the end of tracking (window_end, or the last message when the stream ends before it). The L3 cancellation counters stop at the L3 fill.
Fill fraction at horizon tau uses only shadows with arrival + tau <= end of tracking, whatever their outcome; Kaplan-Meier uses every placed shadow with right censoring.

engine.checkpoint_semantics: State after all messages timestamped <= checkpoint, excluding paths already filled by then; cancellation counters likewise include all messages at the horizon, stopping at the L3 fill.
engine.deadline_semantics: A fill with elapsed <= horizon counts, including every message at the longest deadline; the frozen window end remains exclusive.

definitions.h0: per model and cell: nominal/exploratory rejection when the Newcombe nominal 95% interval excludes 0; no multiplicity adjustment
definitions.h_a: nominal/exploratory support in a cell when the Newcombe nominal 95% interval of RiskAdverse minus L3 lies entirely below 0
definitions.h_b_closer: a probability model is descriptively closer than RiskAdverse in a cell when |its difference| < |RiskAdverse's difference| (point estimates)
definitions.h_b_no_single_model: nominal/exploratory criterion holds for (L, tau) when no model has H0 not rejected on every studied symbol

interval_methods.cancelled_volume: pooled ratio of shares through all messages timestamped <= horizon, stopping at L3 fill; no interval
interval_methods.checkpoints: state after all messages timestamped <= checkpoint; mean over shadows unfilled under both paths by then; no interval
interval_methods.difference_95: nominal 95% Newcombe (1998) method 10 for paired proportions (model minus L3 on the same shadows): Wilson margins, continuity-corrected phi
interval_methods.fill_fraction_95: nominal 95% Wilson score interval (no continuity correction) over eligible shadows
interval_methods.km: Kaplan-Meier product-limit over every placed shadow, right-censored at the horizon or the end of tracking; nominal 95% Greenwood normal interval clipped to [0,1]; median = first time survival <= 0.5

interval_note: Intervals are nominal 95%: overlapping horizons and serially dependent shadows are not accounted for, so coverage is not established. Hypothesis decisions are nominal/exploratory and unadjusted for multiple comparisons.
labels: synthetic: invented ITCH-format messages from the l3-demo generator, not exchange data
L3 reference is reconstructed, shadow fills are counterfactual
shadow orders have no market impact and nobody reacts to them; fills are upper-bound-style model outputs, never recorded executions
latency L is a swept assumption, not calibrated; there is no receipt clock
L2 models apply hftbacktest 0.9.4 queue formulas offline to the L2 projection of the same messages
